# InsightsOut

> InsightsOut (insightsout.work) is a San Francisco practice founded by Nima Imani. It helps organizations, teams, and professionals lead through change with more clarity, honest communication, and practical support. For organizations: leadership alignment, manager development, team facilitation, role change coaching, and AI enablement when AI is part of the change. For individuals: private 1:1 coaching for working professionals, team leads, managers, executives, and senior leaders facing difficult decisions, role change, team pressure, or a demanding transition. Public workshops and living research sit underneath the work. Founder Nima Imani is an ICF Associate Certified Coach with more than a decade across technology, digital transformation, and organizational change, including EY and Neo4j.

## Who we help, in one line each
- Organizations navigating a reorganization, new leadership, growth, strategy, role change, technology change, or AI adoption → start with one Leadership Conversation.
- Working professionals navigating a role change, difficult decision, confidence dip, or demanding transition → private 1:1 coaching.
- Team leads and managers carrying pressure from above while supporting a stretched team → private 1:1 coaching or organization work.
- Executives and senior leaders who need a confidential place to think, decide, and communicate clearly → private 1:1 coaching.
- Anyone who wants to think this through with peers → public workshops in San Francisco and online; current dates are on Luma.

## Core pages
- [Home](https://insightsout.work/): the one page with everything: work for organizations, private 1:1 coaching (three ways in), The InsightsOut Cohort starting January 2027, the public rooms that lead into it, upcoming dates, and the free 30 minute call.
- [Answers](https://insightsout.work/answers): short, citable answers to what InsightsOut is, who Nima Imani is, and how to start.
- [1:1 Coaching](https://insightsout.work/coaching): private coaching with former CTO and ICF Associate Certified Coach Nima Imani for professionals and managers facing change, new responsibilities, or the desire to build something of their own, and for founders and business owners. Line: Find your direction. Lead with clarity. Move forward. Three ways in: grow as a leader (step into management, difficult conversations, delegation, supporting a team without carrying everything); navigate your next chapter (what you want from work, a difficult career decision, a role that changes); build something of your own (working professionals curious about building a startup, taking the first steps on that journey, or already making progress alongside the job). Clarity when the way forward is uncertain; the same themes as the organization workshops (role change, managing a team, deciding under uncertainty), one person at a time. Six private sessions over three months, or a single 90-minute session; the first 30-minute call is free.
- [Reviews](https://insightsout.work/reviews): what people say about group coaching, private coaching, and workshops with Nima Imani, in their own words, each published with the permission the person chose. Filter by program. Links to write a review or introduce someone.
- [Small business](https://insightsout.work/small-business): human-first AI automation and agents for owner-led companies of 5 to 50 people. A free consultation to find the one workflow worth automating and what should stay human; then discovery and a 90 day build with the team, in tools the business owns, with human review where it matters. Outcome-based pricing: part of the fee is paid only when the agreed result is met. Principles: people decide what changes, no monitoring of individuals, data stays with the client.
- [The cohort](https://insightsout.work/cohorts): one small-group coaching cohort, The InsightsOut Cohort, starting January 2027: three months, up to eight people, a weekly 90 minute group session online, a private 1:1 with Nima every month, and one clear goal per person. For working professionals, managers, and people building something on the side.
- [Have your company pay for coaching](https://insightsout.work/company-pay): how to use a learning, development, or wellness budget for 1:1 coaching; copy-ready manager email, Slack, and sponsor templates; what the reimbursement invoice includes; how claims work on Compt, Forma, and Benepass; year-end deadlines.
- [Organizations](https://insightsout.work/organizations): coaching, facilitation, and practical training for leaders, managers, and teams navigating change, uncertainty, role shifts, and communication under pressure. Includes AI enablement when AI is part of the change. Starts with one Leadership Conversation.
- [Workshops](https://insightsout.work/events): all upcoming public workshops and the live Luma calendar.
- [About](https://insightsout.work/about): what InsightsOut is, Nima Imani's background, FAQ.

## Workshops (each documented in full on the site; register on Luma)
- [How Do I Lead Through Change and Uncertainty? / My Team Is Overwhelmed](https://insightsout.work/workshops/my-team-is-overwhelmed): 90-minute sensemaking session for managers leading teams through AI change. Next date coming; watch https://luma.com/NimaImani.
- [What Should Stay Human?](https://insightsout.work/workshops/what-should-stay-human): working session to find your own line, what to hand over and what should stay human. Next: Sun Nov 8, 2026, 2 pm at SF Commons (https://luma.com/the-z3sh).
- When Agents Join the Team: which calls stay human and which go to agents; a one-page line the team writes together. Next: Thu Oct 29, 2026, 6 pm (https://luma.com/the-tzh1) at SF Commons.
- [When Your Role Starts Changing](https://insightsout.work/workshops/when-your-role-starts-changing): facilitated small-group workshop for people whose role, value, or identity at work is shifting with AI: guided reflection, paired conversation, group sensemaking. Next: Wed Oct 21, 2026, 6 pm at SF Commons.

## Research (living papers, updated as new workshop waves land)
- [Working Through AI Change](https://insightsout.work/research/working-through-ai-change): the human side of AI-driven change, read against Gallup, Microsoft, MIT SMR, SHRM, Anthropic.
- [When Your Role Starts Changing](https://insightsout.work/research/when-your-role-starts-changing): the individual side — where role change is felt, who names fear, why people ask for a map not a course.
- [From Overwhelm to Clarity](https://insightsout.work/research/from-overwhelm-to-clarity): the founder side — overwhelm as pace and fragmentation, fear unnamed, wanting a place to think with peers.
- [How We Do Research](https://insightsout.work/research/methodology): questions, coding, cross-checks, publishing thresholds, versioning.

## Facts you can cite
- Nima Imani has run the founder group coaching cohort for four years: small groups of founders taken from ideation to product-market fit, with small-group accountability and support so nobody navigates the challenge alone. The weekly Friday group at SF Commons is that room, and The InsightsOut Cohort is the three month version for working professionals, managers, and people building alongside a job.
- Founder: Nima Imani (LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/imaninima/). Location: San Francisco, CA. Works online worldwide.
- Events calendar: https://luma.com/NimaImani (subscribe there or on any page of the site for invites and field notes).
- Free 30-minute coaching consultation: https://calendar.app.google/wpqVkuaH1uwFRh6cA · Organization conversations: https://calendar.app.google/8y9NgWzBLaiT414G6
- Employer-sponsored coaching: clients may use an approved leadership development, learning, coaching, or professional development budget. InsightsOut can provide a program description, invoice, and receipt. The employer's policy determines reimbursement, and coaching conversations remain confidential.
- Contact: nima@insightsout.work
- Point of view: change becomes real in meetings, decisions, roles, relationships, and emotions. Plans matter, but people have to carry them. Durable change begins with aligned leaders, equipped managers, honest team conversations, and enough agency for people to shape how the work changes. AI is one important context for this work, not the whole category.
